title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Strategy 2026: Pattern, Section Plan and Preparation Roadmap
description: SSC CGL Tier 2 strategy for 2026: Paper 1 pattern out of 390, section-wise approach, marking maths, Computer and DEST, and a 10-week roadmap after Tier 1.
intro: **Tier 2 Paper 1 decides your merit**, because Tier 1 only shortlists you. It is longer, harder and marked more sharply (+3 for correct, -1 for wrong), and English alone carries 135 of the 390 merit marks. This guide covers what the paper looks like, how to split your time, and how to use the weeks between the tiers.

sections.title: Tier 2 Paper 1 pattern
sections.body:
| Module | Questions | Marks | Counts for merit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mathematical Abilities | 30 | 90 | Yes |
| Reasoning and General Intelligence | 30 | 90 | Yes |
| English Language and Comprehension | 45 | 135 | Yes |
| General Awareness | 25 | 75 | Yes |
| Computer Knowledge | 20 | 60 | Qualifying only |
| **Merit total** | **130** | **390** | |

- Marking: **+3 for each correct answer, -1 for each wrong answer**; unanswered questions carry no penalty.
- Paper 1 runs in two sessions. Maths and Reasoning share a 60-minute block, English and General Awareness share another 60-minute block, and the Computer module is 15 minutes (qualifying).
- Reports on the 2026 notice mention sectional caps within those blocks (30 minutes each for Maths and Reasoning, 40 for English and 20 for GA). Confirm the exact timers on the notice and your admit card, and plan your pace to these caps either way.
- The second session includes the **Data Entry Speed Test (DEST)**: 2000 key depressions in 15 minutes, qualifying only.
- **Paper 2 (Statistics, 100 questions, 200 marks, 2 hours)** applies only to JSO aspirants.
- Section-wise qualifying minimums apply, so a weak section can end your candidature even with a high total. Check the [exam pattern](/exams/ssc-cgl/exam-pattern/) page and the SSC notice for the current minimums.

sections.title: Marking maths: when to guess, when to skip
sections.body:
Each question has four options. A blind guess has a 25% chance of being right, so the expected value is 0.25 x 3 - 0.75 x 1 = **0**. In other words, random guessing neither gains nor loses marks in Tier 2.

| Options you can eliminate (correct one stays) | Chance of being right | Expected marks per attempt |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (blind) | 25% | 0 |
| 1 | 33% | about +0.33 |
| 2 | 50% | +1.0 |

The rule: **attempt only when you can eliminate at least one option, and prefer to eliminate two**. This is tighter than Tier 1, where a wrong answer costs only 0.5 against +2. One wrong answer wipes out one-third of a correct answer's reward, so accuracy of at least 80% is the aim, not mass attempts.

sections.title: Maths and Reasoning (Section I)
sections.body:
**Maths (30 questions, 90 marks).** Tier 2 questions are longer and mix concepts. Prioritise the blocks that carry the most questions on our topic data: [Geometry](/quant/geometry/), [Data Interpretation](/quant/data-interpretation/), [Algebra](/quant/algebra/), [Statistics](/quant/statistics/) and [Trigonometry](/quant/trigonometry/), followed by mensuration, percentage and profit-loss.

- **Order of attack** (30 minutes or the equivalent share of your block): first pass for questions you can finish in 45 seconds; second pass for DI sets and geometry; leave heavy calculation for last.
- **Do not chase one question** beyond about 90 seconds; a wrong answer costs 1 and the time costs more.
- Practise with options in mind: back-solving, digit sums and percentage-fraction conversions are the fastest ways to eliminate options.

**Reasoning (30 questions, 90 marks).** Reasoning is usually the best place to bank marks. Do the pattern types first ([Series](/reasoning/series/), [Analogy](/reasoning/analogy/), [Classification](/reasoning/classification/), [Coding-Decoding](/reasoning/coding-decoding/)), then puzzles and sets, then figure-based questions you can solve in seconds. Skip long arrangement puzzles until the end.

If Maths and Reasoning share a 60-minute block, a common split is 30 to 32 minutes for Maths and the rest for Reasoning, adjusting for your strength; if the notice enforces 30 minutes each, drill to those caps.

sections.title: English and General Awareness (Section II)
sections.body:
**English (45 questions, 135 marks)** is the biggest module, so improving it is the best return on time in the Tier 2 window.

- Biggest blocks: [Reading Comprehension](/english/reading-comprehension/), grammar-based questions ([Error spotting](/english/error-spotting/), [Sentence improvement](/english/sentence-improvement/)), [Cloze Test](/english/cloze-test/) and [Fill in the blanks](/english/fill-in-the-blanks/), plus vocabulary ([Synonyms and antonyms](/english/synonyms-antonyms/), [Idioms](/english/idioms-phrases/), [One-word substitution](/english/one-word-substitution/)).
- **Order:** vocabulary and idioms first (quick), then grammar, then cloze, then comprehension passages last. This banks the fast marks before the long reading.
- **Pace:** about 40 minutes if the sectional cap is in force, which means under a minute per question on average. Read passages once, then answer using keywords.
- Use [vocab](/vocab/) for daily words, and read one editorial or long article every day.

**General Awareness (25 questions, 75 marks).** Mostly a memory section; each question takes 20 to 40 seconds if you know it. Give it a 20-minute cap and do not spend time on questions you do not know. Current affairs and Biology lead the shift counts on the [weightage](/exams/ssc-cgl/weightage/) page; revise the last 8 to 12 months of [current affairs](/current-affairs/) in the final weeks.

sections.title: Computer Knowledge and the data-entry speed test
sections.body:
Both are qualifying only, but failing either ends your candidature, so they deserve fixed small slots.

- **Computer Knowledge (20 questions, 15 minutes).** Basics only: fundamentals, hardware and memory, MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, internet and email, networking and cyber security. Revise from [Computer Fundamentals](/computer/computer-fundamentals/), [MS Excel](/computer/ms-excel/) and [Cyber Security](/computer/cyber-security/). A week of focused revision is enough for most candidates, and a daily 10-minute quiz keeps it fresh.
- **DEST (2000 key depressions in 15 minutes).** Practise 15 to 20 minutes a day on a physical keyboard from the day you clear Tier 1. Phone typing does not transfer. Start practising on the [typing test](/exams/ssc-cgl/typing-test/) page and aim for a comfortable margin over the required speed.

If you are a JSO aspirant, add Paper 2 (Statistics) to your plan.

sections.title: A 10-week roadmap between the tiers
sections.body:
Past cycles left a gap of roughly three to four months between Tier 1 and Tier 2 (see the timeline on the [exam pattern](/exams/ssc-cgl/exam-pattern/) page); the 2026 Tier 2 date is not announced yet. If your gap is shorter, compress by merging weeks 2 and 3, and 5 and 6. Study 6 to 7 hours a day.

| Weeks | Maths | Reasoning | English | GA, Computer, DEST |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Review Tier 1 mistakes; arithmetic tests at Tier 2 level | Weak types | Vocabulary list (150 words), grammar rules | Current affairs (all months) |
| 2 to 3 | Geometry, Trigonometry | Puzzles and sets | RC practice, one passage a day | Polity, economy, history |
| 4 to 5 | Algebra, Data Interpretation, Statistics | Non-verbal types | Cloze test, error spotting, sentence improvement | Science; Computer basics; DEST 15 min a day |
| 6 | Mensuration and mixed advanced sets | Mixed timed sets | 45-question timed English sets | Static GK |
| 7 to 8 | Tier 2 style mocks, 3 a week | Mock analysis | Mock analysis | Current affairs revision |
| 9 | Weak-topic repair, 2 mocks | Weak types | Weak areas | DEST at full speed |
| 10 | Light revision, 1 mock at the start of the week | Formula sheet | Vocabulary and idioms | Rest before the exam |

**Target.** The 2024 final-merit cutoffs for the largest posts ran at 332 (AAO, UR) and 318 (ASO, UR) out of 390 according to the [cutoffs](/exams/ssc-cgl/cutoffs/) page; verify against SSC's own PDF, and remember that they change every year with vacancies and difficulty. Aim for strong accuracy in every module and no weak section, rather than a number you cannot control.

faqs.q: What is the Tier 2 pattern for SSC CGL?
faqs.a: Paper 1 has Maths (30 questions), Reasoning (30), English (45) and General Awareness (25) for a merit total of 390 marks, plus a qualifying Computer module (20 questions) and a data-entry speed test. Marking is +3 for each correct answer and -1 for each wrong one.

faqs.q: Is there sectional timing in Tier 2?
faqs.a: Paper 1 is divided into timed blocks: 60 minutes for Maths and Reasoning, 60 minutes for English and General Awareness, and 15 minutes for Computer. Reports on the 2026 notice also mention sectional caps of 30, 30, 40 and 20 minutes within the two blocks. Confirm these on the notice and admit card.

faqs.q: Which module is most important in Tier 2?
faqs.a: English carries the most marks (45 questions, 135 marks), so it is where improvement pays most. Maths is usually the one that separates ranks, and Reasoning is a good place to bank accuracy.

faqs.q: Should I attempt all questions in Tier 2?
faqs.a: No. With +3 and -1, a blind guess has zero expected value. Attempt when you can eliminate at least one option, and aim for accuracy of 80% or more.

faqs.q: Is the Computer test or DEST counted in merit?
faqs.a: No. Both are qualifying only, but you must clear them. DEST requires 2000 key depressions in 15 minutes, so practise on a physical keyboard before the exam.
Paper 2 is the Statistics paper (100 questions, 200 marks, 2 hours) and applies to JSO aspirants only. Other posts are decided on Paper 1.
